Customer: Datadog's main advantage is correlating data across APM, custom metrics and logs via tagging, densely linked across the platform, plus built-in notebooks. Had to use OTel for Elixir apps since there's no DD SDK for Elixir/Erlang. On-demand pricing gets expensive fast, but replicating it self-hosted would require hiring another engineer.
"DataDog Don't Discount": compared to most enterprise vendors it's much harder to get a discount from Datadog; most vendors give ~1/3 off for committing to spend, Datadog doesn't.
Another user says they've never been able to negotiate Datadog down in years; price is always what's on the website, which they don't mind compared to bazaar-style vendor haggling.
Counterpoint: spending a few thousand a month, their account manager adjusts the monthly commit quarterly, giving roughly a 20% discount off website prices.
User at a medium-sized unicorn complains Datadog doesn't default to UTC or clearly label time zones on logs/graphs, causing confusion during prod outages about whether timestamps are PST, CST or UTC.

Notebooks are used for incidents (metrics side by side with comments), long-term reliability debugging, and performance tuning; widgets can be moved between dashboards and notebooks, and state lives in the URL so views are easy to share in Slack.
Critic: Datadog's data correlation is awful compared to Honeycomb, Dynatrace and Instana; users end up sifting through outdated dashboards and notebooks instead of being shown anomalies.

Company spending over $6M/yr left Datadog for Grafana despite leadership being DD fans. DD was easier for everyone, had useful baked-in features (apdex) and let non-devs build dashboards, but they left over lack of billing transparency and an incompetent account rep who angered finance and embarrassed the CTO.
User: Datadog solves a real and burning problem for product engineering teams, and though expensive, is worth every penny.
Long-time customer: the product has always been amazing, absolutely reliable and beautifully designed; they never once flinched at the bill.
Negative experience: difficult setup and tracking, with trace collection much more resource-intensive than New Relic; support emails went unanswered until a coworker complained publicly on Twitter.
Used Datadog and New Relic in large-scale production apps and, for the cost, still not very impressed by the developer experience/UX.
Favourite Datadog features: clicking a field to make it a custom search dimension in one more click, and flame graphs.
Datadog is cool but the price is ridiculously high for small orgs.
Contrasting view: Datadog is one of their favorite providers; pricing is great for small businesses but probably unaffordable for larger ones.
Datadog's server hexagon map chart praised as an innovative, standout visualization.
User wants a local-development "Datadog Lite". Datadog has no local option for verifying tracing and metrics before shipping, and Grafana is too bloated and poorly documented for that use case.
Harsh UI critique: the Datadog interface felt like a product where no one in the org ever said no to an idea, "very Atlassian."

Likes Datadog but finds it prohibitively expensive for monitoring serverless AWS apps, even with negotiated rates; the Datadog bill is many orders of magnitude higher than their AWS bill, so they're looking for alternatives.
Outlier analysis cited as a key advantage of Datadog and New Relic over open-source alternatives.
